pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test 'AC-1' checks the seeded items are all 0 and that 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' expects ["First item","★ Second item","Third item"]; src/index.js item().
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and expects only those, in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give all items in id order with the star in place.
test 'AC-5' checks the exact link in each view.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred; test 'AC-7' asserts it. The traffic-config check and traffic.test.js were updated to accept a query.

findings.what: The last commit ('Follow-up edits') loosened the 'No starred items' state test. `expect(listed(html)).toEqual([])` became `toBeDefined()`. `listed()` always returns an array, so the assertion can never fail. The test no longer checks that the starred view lists nothing, which the state table row 'No starred items' requires. The spec records no justification for loosening it.
The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none'. That is false: the final commit loosened an assertion in the 'No starred items' state test.
findings.fix: Restore the assertion, or state the loosening in the PR body.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec. Starred items keep their place in the list. The view is a query parameter. There is no cookie and no write route. The traffic-check regex change is needed for AC-7.
All 7 ACs are met. All 4 state rows have tests, but the 'No starred items' test was weakened in the last commit (see findings).
One assertion can never fail (toBeDefined on an array). I did not run the suite here; CI runs it.
The README mentions ?show=starred. CLAUDE.md and the README already require new routes in routes.json, and that was done.
Object.hasOwn guards against prototype keys. The SQL is built only from fixed view strings. Output is escaped.
The show input is whitelisted. The title is HTML-escaped. The query string is not interpolated into SQL. The relaxed route regex still refuses spaces and #.
The diff touches no UI files beyond server-rendered HTML in src/index.js. There is no stylesheet, component or screenshot.
There is no browser flow to run in this review. The server-rendered pages are covered by the Worker tests.
The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is false (see findings).
